title: Cycle Forecast Windowing & Skill-Constrained Staffing Guide
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As usage patterns and hiring velocity become less predictable, we need a lightweight, operational forecasting and staffing guide that helps PMs and ENG leads: 1) translate OKRs/initiatives into weekly staffing targets, 2) allocate constrained specialist hours (infra, infra-ops, reliability, design) across tranches, and 3) decide mid-cycle scope cuts with minimal customer and technical risk.

Deliverables:
- A prescriptive 'windowing' technique for smoothing incoming demand across a rolling 3-cycle horizon.
- A skill-constrained staffing matrix and a decision rubric for forced de-scopes.
- A one-page playbook + template (Confluence) and an accompanying lightweight spreadsheet for simulations.

Why now: Recent cycle reviews identified recurring rushed de-scopes and concentration of specialist work in the last week of cycles. This increases rework, decreases velocity predictability, and raises incident risk during rollouts. The guide aims to reduce end-of-cycle churn and provide clearer tradeoffs for PM/ENG leads.

How we will work:
- Run a two-week pilot across two initiatives (runtime-1.18 rollout and console-2026.04 dashboard) to validate signals.
- Use historical cycle data from the Cycle Capacity Dashboard (https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity) to parameterize the model.
- Ship Confluence playbook, a Google Sheets simulator, and a small training session for PMs and Eng managers.

Artifacts and links:
- Draft Playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/Cycle+Forecast+Windowing+Draft
- Simulation template: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ExampleTemplate
- Cycle Capacity dashboard: https://internal.redwood.ai/dashboards/capacity
- Related PRD: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1PRD-Example
- Follow-up GH issue for automation work: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/issues/784
